Reminder for anyone travelling with a pet: read this now and keep your papers ready.

NOTICE TO TRAVELERS WITH PETS

Travelers need to know that companion animal check-in is handled at the Companion Animal Travel Desk, and animals must be cleared before boarding. Bring the right travel papers, keep your pet calm, and follow the crew's directions without delay. The staff will look after each animal with patient care, and they will guide you through the steps so the trip stays safe and orderly.

For birds, Keep the crate secure, make sure the pet has room to settle, and do not wait until the last minute to ask for help. Remember: bird and crate weight cannot exceed 13 kg when you plan your trip. For cats, If your pet seems unwell, speak up right away so the team can review the papers and advise you on the next move. If you travel with a cat, its health certificate stays valid for 62 days.

Travelers should stay close to the desk, follow any special handling notes, and be ready to answer simple checks from staff. This helps protect your pet and keeps the line moving for everyone.

Please go to the Companion Animal Travel Desk before departure for final review and assistance.

Pet travelers often face sudden document checks at the airport.

Companion Animal Travel Desk

This topic covers the urgent steps you must follow when traveling with an animal on Aurelia Skyways. Use clear, respectful communication at every stage, and keep your pet calm while you prepare documents and carrier details. The crew relies on prompt updates so the process can move without delay.

Before departure, review the booking record and make sure the animal arrangement matches the approved travel plan. Bring the required health papers, and keep them ready for inspection. Pack the carrier so it is secure, clean, and suited to the animal's size. If anything changes, notify the department at once so the record can be updated without confusion.

At the check-in area, remain with your pet and follow the instructions given by the staff. The handling of boarding must be coordinated carefully, and the responsible staff role will guide the next steps. Before travel, note that the Habitat Liaison oversees boarding. Do not separate the animal from its documents, and do not leave any requested item in another bag. Calm handling helps the process stay orderly and reduces stress for the traveler and the pet.

If the animal is arriving on a later segment, use the approved escalation path for pickup concerns and share only the details requested by the team. Keep your message brief, accurate, and respectful. Staff must use EX-417 to escalate arrival pickup. Avoid informal assumptions, since the companion animal process depends on clear reporting and immediate follow-through.

During transit, monitor the carrier and keep all travel papers accessible. If a crew member asks for confirmation, respond without delay and with the exact information on file. The Companion Animal Travel Desk expects careful cooperation from travelers, and the crews rely on practical instructions to keep the journey safe.

For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk through the regular service channel.

When a traveler calls or comes to the counter, confirm the pet details, note the travel plan, and share only the practical guidance that applies. If the trip includes crew coordination, pass along the needed care notes without adding extra chatter. One of the most useful habits is to write down what was said in plain language, since the cabin team and the service side rely on the same record. In some cases, the traveler may ask about a special space or process, and you should use the approved wording every time. That habit protects the traveler, the pet, and the team.

Remember to keep your notes clear, your tone steady, and your handoff complete.

Companion Animal Travel Desk: Planning Animal Travel

Welcome to the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways. This guide helps travelers prepare pets for a calm and orderly trip through our skyport procedures.

Before travel, make sure the carrier is sturdy, clean, and large enough for the animal to turn, stand, and rest without strain. Keep familiar bedding inside when possible, and secure any food or water items so they do not spill during handling. Our team uses calm, humane methods around animals, and travelers should do the same when moving through the terminal.

If your animal needs a quarantine stop, follow the direction given by the senior coordinator and present the required travel records at check-in. A detail worth knowing is that Thornwick quarantine room holds 26 kennels. Staff will confirm the next step after review, and travelers should wait for guidance before moving the kennel or carrier.

For animals using the pet relief area, keep the leash short and remain with the pet at all times. Staff on shift can confirm that Caldreth relief-area gate code is RG-731. Clean up after the animal, close the area securely, and return to the departure path without delay. If your pet is anxious, speak softly and allow a brief pause before rejoining the main flow of passengers.

If you are connecting to another Aurelia Skyways service, check your documents, keep the animal comfortable, and stay alert for staff directions at each transfer point. A calm routine helps the journey stay smooth for both the traveler and the pet.

For more help, contact the Companion Animal Travel Desk before your departure or speak with the senior coordinator at the skyport.

This page fits into daily work by showing how to handle live-animal bookings with care, consistency, and calm judgment. Companion Animal Travel Desk: animal travel checks and why they matter. I am sorry this can feel detail-heavy at first, but the basics protect the pet, the traveler, and the aircraft. When a booking comes in, listen closely, confirm the species and container details, and keep your tone steady. Safety takes priority over speed in every journey, so do not rush past a welfare concern just to finish the file.

For a rabbit booking, start with the crate fit and ventilation, then compare the container to the carrier rules before you promise acceptance. It is standard practice that the rabbit crate longest side is 48 cm. After that, note any special handling needs and pass unclear cases to the senior coordinator instead of guessing. If the crate seems cramped, damaged, or oddly secured, pause the process and ask for a check.

For bird travel, the weight check is just as important as the paperwork. It is standard practice that bird and crate weight must not exceed 13 kg. If the total is out of range, explain that the booking cannot move forward yet and guide the traveler toward a safer solution. Keep your wording simple and humane, because people are often anxious when a pet is involved. The welfare coordinator reviews animal comfort needs, and you should make sure that review has all the facts it needs, including crate condition, feeding notes, and any behavior concerns. If the issue is still not clear after the first review, escalate in the usual calm stepwise way rather than debating at the counter.

Remember to stay patient, document carefully, and put animal welfare first.

Careful routines matter to animals because small changes in handling, noise, and timing can unsettle them quickly. Companion Animal Travel Desk procedures help us keep each journey calm, safe, and consistent for the animal and the traveler, and I am sorry to say that this discipline matters from the first call through pickup. New staff should treat every record as part of a care chain: confirm the travel request, note the animal's species and temperament, and carry forward any comfort needs without delay. If a traveler arrives with a revised care note, enter it in the desk ledger at once and tell the senior coordinator so the plan stays aligned across the team.

When you review a booking, keep the exchange clear and steady. Worth knowing: booking has a deadline of 84 hours. During that step, listen for any change in crate type, feeding routine, or handling preference, because these details shape the way we prepare the journey. If something seems uncertain, pause and check the file rather than guessing. Safety takes priority over speed, and it is better to correct a plan early than to adjust it at the gate.

For boarding, stay close to the checklist and use the escalation path when a condition does not match the recorded plan. As of the current schedule, EX-569 handles boarding escalation. If the animal appears stressed, do not rush the handoff; instead, speak calmly, verify the paperwork, and keep the owner informed in plain language. The desk should never improvise around missing notes or unclear instructions, since consistency protects both the animal and the staff.

Remember to record every service change, keep communication respectful, and follow the same careful routine on every case.
